title: TMCP can_do input
description: Input contract for the can_do tool. Accepts a structured intent query and returns a CapabilityReport (see capability-report.json). can_do is the single generic tool in the TMCP triad — it takes semantic intent, not a capability-specific name. It is the plan-before-act primitive.

intent.description: Structured description of the desired action.

semantic_tags.description: One or more tags describing the capability category being sought. These are matched against the server's capability declarations. Examples: ['inventory', 'transfer'], ['temperature', 'hvac', 'zone_3'], ['claim', 'submit', 'healthcare'].

action.description: The intended action direction. Optional but improves candidate ranking precision. 'read' should not appear here — use read_* tools directly. Use 'set' for absolute values, 'increase'/'decrease' for relative adjustments.

target.description: The property, resource, or entity being targeted. Examples: 'stock_location', 'fan_speed', 'claim_status', 'temperature_setpoint'.

value.description: Optional target value. When provided, candidates will include constraint information to indicate whether the value is within bounds.

location.description: Logical scope for the query. Used to filter candidates by zone, region, resource group, or any other location identifier declared in capability metadata. Examples: 'zone_3', 'warehouse_A', 'us-east-1'.

scope.description: Optional list of capability names or source identifiers to constrain the search. When provided, only listed capabilities are evaluated. Useful when the orchestrator already knows the target tool but needs a current permission and validity check.
